skill.name: agent-tools
skill.description: Use the inference.sh belt CLI to discover and run cloud AI apps for image, video, LLM, search, 3D, and social workflows.
skill.summary: Run inference.sh cloud AI apps from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code workflows.
skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: The skill is mostly documentation for the inference.sh belt CLI, but it includes confirmed critical curl-to-shell installer patterns and persistent binary installation guidance. Many Markdown links, API key placeholders, and shell-completion examples are benign, while local file uploads and social media automation create real data and account-action risks. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell examples with download, inspect, checksum, signature verification, and explicit execution steps.

remediation.issue: Manual install places a downloaded executable into the user PATH.
remediation.suggestion: Pin releases, require signature verification, and ask for explicit confirmation before installing binaries into ~/.local/bin.

remediation.issue: Local file paths can be uploaded to hosted apps.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval for each file path and restrict uploads to intended workspace files.

remediation.issue: Twitter/X automation can publish or change account state.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before posts, messages, follows, likes, or retweets, and document required account permissions.

remediation.issue: API key setup examples may lead to unsafe secret handling.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend secret managers or CI secret stores and warn users not to paste real keys into prompts or logs.

content.value_statement: Teams often need one interface for many hosted AI models. This skill guides agents through the inference.sh CLI for discovery, execution, and task tracking.
actual_capabilities: Guides installation and login for the inference.sh belt CLI.
Lists commands for browsing, searching, and filtering public AI apps.
Shows how to run named apps with inline input or saved input files.
Explains task tracking for long-running image, video, and audio jobs.
Documents local media uploads for compatible cloud AI apps.
Links related skills and official inference.sh documentation.
limitations: Requires the belt CLI and an inference.sh account or API key.
Runs hosted services, so results depend on quotas, model availability, and provider latency.
Local file paths can upload files to cloud apps and require explicit user approval.
The skill documents commands but does not verify every app schema itself.

use_cases.title: Prototype AI Media Workflows
use_cases.description: Find and run image, video, audio, or 3D apps without managing local GPU infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Run Model Tasks from an Agent
use_cases.description: Use Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to select an app, prepare input, submit a job, and check results.

use_cases.title: Compare Search and LLM Providers
use_cases.description: Browse OpenRouter, Tavily, Exa, and other hosted apps for repeatable research workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Generate an Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use inference.sh to find an image generation app and create a clean product image. Ask before using any local file.

prompt_templates.title: Discover Matching Apps
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the inference.sh app store for web search tools and compare three options by purpose, input needs, and output type.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Media Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a safe video generation workflow using an approved image file, submit it with belt, and monitor the task until completion.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Multi-Step Research
prompt_templates.prompt: Use inference.sh apps to search the web, summarize findings with a Claude model, and draft a social post without publishing it.

output_examples.input: A designer asks for a concept image using a hosted image model.
output_examples.output: The agent selects a suitable image app, confirms the prompt, submits the task, and returns the result link.

output_examples.input: A researcher wants recent information and a concise summary.
output_examples.output: The agent compares search apps, runs the selected provider, and summarizes the findings with source-aware context.

output_examples.input: A team needs a long-running video job monitored.
output_examples.output: The agent starts the job, records the task identifier, checks status, and reports when the output is ready.

best_practices: Review installer scripts, checksums, and signatures before installing the CLI.
Use scoped API keys and keep secrets out of shared prompts, logs, and saved files.
Confirm before uploading local files or performing social media actions.
anti_patterns: Piping remote installer scripts directly to a shell without review.
Uploading personal files, parent directories, or broad paths without explicit consent.
Letting an agent publish posts, send messages, or follow accounts automatically.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps agents use the inference.sh belt CLI to discover apps, run hosted AI tasks, and track results.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run models locally?
faq.answer: No. It sends tasks to hosted inference.sh apps and returns cloud results.

faq.question: Does it upload local files?
faq.answer: Yes, compatible apps can upload local paths. Users should approve each file before submission.

faq.question: Do I need credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI requires login or an INFSH_API_KEY value for authenticated use.

faq.question: Is installation risk-free?
faq.answer: No. The documentation includes remote installer commands, so users should inspect and verify downloads before running them.
